title: Immunization Services Cash Dose Charge Schedule
content:
# Immunization Services — Cash Dose Charge Schedule

**Schedule rule.** For a vaccine dose of Kestrel Pharmacy's Immunization Services that is paid in cash, the charge is the vaccination's cash price, rounded to the cent half up.

The vaccination's cash price is the cash price per dose, administration included, that the Immunization Services price schedule lists for the vaccination the course is for. The starting price of the charge is that cash price.

**How the charge is formed.** The Savings Club discount, the coverage continuity reduction and the pharmacy-patient reduction are first added into one total reduction percent, which is then held to the cap; the starting price is reduced once by that capped total, the on-time credit is subtracted from the reduced price, the result is never below zero, and it is rounded to the cent half up only at the end.

Read as a definition of each quantity:

| Quantity | Definition |
|---|---|
| Starting price | The vaccination's cash price |
| Total reduction percent | The three reduction percents added together, or the cap where their total is above the cap |
| Reduced price | The starting price multiplied by one hundred percent less the total reduction percent, applied once to the starting price |
| Charge before rounding | The reduced price less the on-time credit in dollars, or zero where that would be below zero |
| Charge | The charge before rounding, rounded to the cent half up, once, at the end |

The percents are added together first, and their capped total acts once, on the starting price. No figure is rounded before the last line.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

The figures below are hypothetical inputs chosen to show the arithmetic; they are not prices, percents or credits of any vaccination or patient.

**Example A — no reduction percent and no credit on the dose.** Hypothetical cash price 44.625 dollars. The starting price is 44.625 dollars, the reduced price is the same, and the charge is 44.625 dollars rounded to the cent half up: **44.63 dollars**.

**Example B — percents held to the cap.** Hypothetical starting price 150.00 dollars; hypothetical reduction percents of 12, 15 and 8 add to 35 percent; hypothetical cap 30 percent, so the total reduction percent is 30. Reduced price: 150.00 multiplied by 70 percent, which is 105.00 dollars. Hypothetical credit 4.00 dollars: 105.00 less 4.00 is 101.00. Charge: **101.00 dollars**.

**Example C — rounding only at the end.** Hypothetical starting price 45.25 dollars; hypothetical total reduction percent 10, within a hypothetical cap. Reduced price: 45.25 multiplied by 90 percent, which is 40.725 dollars. No credit. Rounded to the cent half up at the end: **40.73 dollars**.

**Example D — never below zero.** Hypothetical starting price 20.00 dollars; hypothetical total reduction percent 80. Reduced price 4.00 dollars; hypothetical credit 7.50 dollars. 4.00 less 7.50 would be below zero, so the charge is **0.00 dollars**.

## Schedule notes

- The reduction acts once, on the starting price, by the capped total percent.
- The credit is taken off the reduced price, never off the starting price.
- Rounding to the cent, half up, happens once, on the final figure.
